text:
Marta: Heads-up — during the quant4b bring-up we saw a weird cluster of collisions in the seedpool merge. looks like a small set of inputs with an extra leading sigil (">>#") are bypassing our fuzzyhash dedupe and getting assigned to multiple cohorts.
Ashwin: Ugh. Sigils again. Are they from upstream scraping or some export artifact?
Marta: Preliminary inspection — looks like two ingestion pipelines: web-scrape v2 (no clean-step) and partner dump (legacy). partner dump sometimes prefixes agent markers like >># or %% to mark system text. those markers are leaking into prompts.
Joyce: That explains the hash mismatches. Our fingerprinting normalizes whitespace but not arbitrary prefixes. We should strip known sigils before hashing.
Sam: Quick mitigation: can we add a prehash normalizer that strips ^(>>#|%%|__SIGIL__) tokens and then re-run dedupe for the last 48h window? low risk and reversible.
Marta: Agreed. Also need to avoid changing golden set semantics — some golds intentionally include markup (eg code fences). We should only strip markers when they match the ingestion provenance flag.
Label-bot: NOTE: If dedupe changes, active label batches with IDs 42/43 may see sample shifts. Pause auto-assign? :warning:
Natalie: Good catch. Let's snapshot current label batches and golden membership before any mass re-hash. I can export batch manifests now.
Ashwin: Action plan:
1) Marta to add sigil-strip filter behind feature flag (feature: sigil_normalize).
2) Natalie to export current golden & active label manifests.
3) Joyce to run a small re-hash on a 10k canary and diff assignments.
4) Sam to hold label-assigner autoscale until we confirm no churn.
Can we commit to that today?
Marta: I’ll open a PR for the filter and gate it with an env var. Patch will include a whitelist for allowed markers and an opt-out annotation per-sample. PR in ~1h.
Joyce: I ran the local canary on 10k: results — dedupe rate increases by 1.8% and 97% of reassignments are duplicates of existing samples. No golden sample collisions in the canary but a handful of labeler-assigned candidates changed bucket. I'll paste diff in a follow-up.
Sam: If canary looks clean, what about quant bench impact? could dedupe shift alter distribution seen by quant kernels (seqlen distribution)?
Marta: Good flag. We'll snapshot token length histograms pre/post. If we see >2% shift in mean seqlen for any model, rollback.
Natalie: Export done. Manifests stored at s3://rf-curation/snapshots/1755550001-manifest.json (internal link).
Ashwin: One more thought — onboard tests for new models should check ingest normalization parity. Add a lint step in model-onboard: "ingest-normalization-vs-production" to catch these markers early.
Marta: OK will add lint and a short doc in the curation handbook about sigils and partner dumps. PR: https://git.internal/rf/curation/pulls/512 (:link:).
Joyce: After PR merges, I'll run full 48h backfill dry-run against staging, produce assignment deltas and per-labeler change counts. If anything >5% churn for a labeler we pause.
Sam: Thanks everyone. Ping me when you want me to pause assigner autoscale — I’ll script the temp hold. :thumbsup:
Marta: Wrapping up — primary goal: avoid golden set regressions while removing noisy duplicates. will post final diffs and action summary once staging dry-run completes.
Ashwin: Nice coord. tagging infra for quick rollback hooks if needed.
Label-bot: REMINDER: please annotate any sample with provenance tag "partner_dump" if it was modified by this normalization — helps audits.
Marta: Noted, will add transform metadata.
